key_insight: MESH-Harness improves fixed-language-model agent performance by evolving the harness itself through modular recombination, bandit-guided selection, and feedback-driven edits.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that agent control logic can be optimized as an engineering artifact under tight evaluation budgets, reducing both search cost and test-time cost without changing model weights.
method: Break the harness into role-specific modules with swappable implementations.
Score candidate module combinations with shared representations and full-covariance LinUCB.
Use mixed-start coordinate ascent plus validation-trace-guided local edits, then recycle strong modules into fixed-capacity pools.
evidence_signal: Across text, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and interactive scientific tasks, MESH-Harness beats Meta-Harness by 2.00 to 7.01 points under matched evaluation budgets, with 44.2% lower aggregate test-time cost and 14.6% lower total cost including search.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful module decomposition and pool management, so gains may be sensitive to how well the harness is factored and how representative the validation traces are.
paper_title: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution
